description: The Open Database of Infrastructure is a harmonised national collection of open datasets giving the types and locations of selected infrastructure across Canada. Version 2 includes 14 infrastructure types in three categories, energy (electrical grid, low carbon infrastructure, oil and gas), transport (airports, bridges and tunnels, ports and marinas, railways, pedestrian, cycling and public transit networks) and utilities (potable water, solid waste, telecommunications, wastewater and stormwater), with common variables such as provider, source ID, province, census subdivision and geometry; its data were collected between October 2023 and June 2024. It is compiled by Statistics Canada from municipal, regional, provincial and national open data, as part of the Linkable Open Data Environment, and was released on 13 November 2024. Each type is available as a free compressed download with a GeoPackage, a record layout CSV, a data providers CSV and a metadata PDF, under the Open Government Licence - Canada, and can be viewed in the LODE Viewer. Caveats: geographic coverage varies by type with the licensing and availability of source data. It supports multi-sector exposure and network studies in Canada; a related record is the Canadian critical infrastructure interdependency metrics.
